description:
Similarweb Group Buy is an option to compare if you need competitor traffic research and want to check a discounted offer before paying for a full subscription. Start with one decision you need to make. You might want to see which countries bring traffic to competing stores, which channels deserve more research, or which websites attract visitors for the same keywords. A focused comparison gives you something useful to act on before you open another report.

Similarweb offers its own packages. This SEOGBTools listing is a separate offer. If you are comparing a Similarweb shared account, check how access works, which reports are included, and which limits apply. Confirm the available country filters, history, exports, and support before you order. These details matter when a client project requires a particular report.

What does Similarweb show?

Similarweb estimates website traffic and provides reports that can help you compare websites. Depending on the report and package, you may be able to explore visits, engagement, traffic sources, and geography. Its search research features also help you examine the keywords associated with a site and identify websites that compete for similar searches. Similarweb website performance guide

For your own website, use first-party tools when you need the site's measured performance. Search Console can show Google search clicks and impressions. An analytics setup can help you understand how people use the site, subject to how it collects data. Similarweb estimates can be useful for comparing other websites when you do not have access to their private analytics.

Use the tool to support a decision rather than to collect numbers for their own sake. A freelance SEO might compare the sources of competitor visits before recommending research priorities. An ecommerce owner might compare the countries where two stores appear to be active. An agency might investigate whether relevant competitors rely more on search, referrals, or paid campaigns. Each job needs a clear question and a comparable group of sites.

Choose competitors you can compare fairly

Start with two or three websites serving a similar audience. A store selling office furniture in one country can learn more from other stores with similar products and delivery areas than from a marketplace operating in dozens of countries. A larger site can still be a useful reference, but write down what makes it different before interpreting the numbers.

Choose the same country, period, and device scope where those options are available. If one site gets most of its visits from a market you do not serve, a global comparison can make its performance look more relevant than it is. Compare the market you can actually reach. Record the filters and date so you can repeat the check later.

There are several kinds of competitors. A business competitor serves the same customers. A search competitor appears for queries you want to target. A referral competitor may earn attention from publishers or communities you also care about. A site can belong to more than one group. Choose the group that answers the current question instead of using the same list for every report.

Read traffic sources in context

A channel report helps you compare the estimated mix of visits associated with channels such as organic search, paid search, direct, social, and referrals. Look at both the mix and the scale of each website. A large share for one channel can mean that it dominates a smaller site's traffic. Another site may have a smaller share of that channel and still receive more visits from it.

Use the result to pick a follow-up. If a competitor appears to get a large share of visits from search, look at the relevant queries and pages. If referral traffic stands out, look for the types of websites sending attention and how those sites discuss the business. If paid traffic appears substantial, review the landing pages and public offers before assuming that more ad spending is the answer.

Avoid drawing a conclusion from one period alone. A promotion, a product launch, or a seasonal shift can change a traffic mix. Compare similar months where possible and look for repeatable patterns. If the report changes significantly, write down what else might explain it. You can investigate a hypothesis without claiming you know what happened inside a competitor's business.

Compare audience geography before picking a market

Use the geography report to see how estimated traffic is distributed across countries where the package allows it. A global report may help you see where a competitor attracts attention. A country-level comparison can be more useful when you are deciding where to write a local guide, improve delivery information, or research a campaign.

For example, a furniture store serving only the United Kingdom should compare relevant UK websites before making decisions about products or delivery. A competitor may get a large share of global visits from another country. That does not tell you whether UK buyers want the same products or use the same search terms. Open relevant results in the target market and check prices, measurements, and availability before writing.

Check which countries are included in your access and how much history you can see. If an estimate is unavailable, record it as unavailable. Use other public evidence and your own data rather than assuming the missing figure represents zero visits. Keep the scope narrow enough that you can verify the examples you use in a report.

Use competitor keywords to find a real gap

Start with a page or category you own. Choose a couple of competitors that appear for a relevant search and look at their keyword coverage where available. Similarweb's website keyword reports can help you explore overlap and opportunities. Review a shortlist by hand before deciding that a phrase needs a new page. Similarweb Website Keywords documentation

Group phrases by what the searcher needs. A phrase such as compact office desk may lead to product collections. How to measure a desk for a small room may lead to guides. A question about delivery may belong near the purchase controls or on the shipping page. If several phrases call for the same answer, group them instead of creating several pages that repeat it.

Compare the opportunity with your own site. If a category already appears for some related searches, check whether the page can answer more of the relevant questions. A size chart or product filter may help visitors more than a new article. If a separate guide serves a distinct task, explain the topic with a useful example and link to the category when the reader is ready to browse.

Work through a competitor research example

Imagine a small online shop sells compact desks. The team wants to understand where other stores attract shoppers who are setting up a home office. Start with stores that sell a comparable range and deliver to the same market. Compare the estimated channels for the same period. If search appears important, find a few relevant queries and open the landing pages.

Suppose several competing stores have categories for narrow desks, while the shop lists them within a larger office collection. Check the shop's inventory and the current results. If enough models fit the category, a dedicated page might help shoppers compare widths and prices. If the selection is small, clear dimensions and a link from a measuring guide may be more practical.

Write down one proposed change and how you will evaluate it. Add the date, target page, related queries, and what a visitor should be able to do after opening it. Verify the public page and its internal links after launch. Then compare the site's own impressions and clicks over a meaningful period. Keep any competitor estimate as background to the decision.

What does Similarweb global rank mean?

Similarweb global rank is one of the comparative ranking signals the vendor provides for websites. It can help place a site in a wider comparison, but it does not explain whether a website attracts the particular visitors you want. Check the local market, the channel mix, and relevant competitors when you need to make a marketing decision. Similarweb Traffic and Engagement documentation

Keep the meaning of rank clear when reporting to a client. A website rank from a competitive intelligence platform and a position for one Google query describe different things. Use a position report when you want to monitor a specific search and landing page. Use competitive traffic reports when you want a broader picture of how websites compare.

Avoid treating small differences as decisive. A comparison can reveal a pattern worth investigating, especially when several signals point in the same direction. For smaller websites, check whether the data is available and how it is described. Use public pages and first-party evidence wherever possible to confirm the part of the picture you can verify.

Check discounted access before ordering

Ask which reports are included in this Similarweb group buy offer. If you need a country filter, the history for a competitor, or an export for a client report, ask about that exact workflow. Check the access period and how support works if the service is interrupted. Confirm the price at checkout and compare it with the official package that covers the same tasks.

If your main goal is to look up a few public websites, try the public traffic checker before deciding what you need from paid access. For recurring work, test a representative public comparison. Check that you can choose the market, see the metrics you need, and save a usable record. Ask about seats and project visibility if more than one person needs access or if work must be kept separate.

If you need competitor keywords and broader SEO workflows, compare Semrush Group Buy. For another keyword gap workflow, see Serpstat Group Buy. Use the same domain and market when comparing tools so the difference you observe is relevant to the work you want to do.

Keep a short research record

For each comparison, write down the site, country, device scope, date range, and report used. Add a column for the question the report is meant to answer. Keep estimates and verified observations in separate columns. For example, record the estimated traffic mix in one place and the actual landing pages you opened in another.

Give the report an owner and a next step. A developer might need to improve a filter. A writer might need to answer a delivery question. A marketer might need to check whether a referral source is relevant to the business. A useful comparison should give the next person enough evidence to check the idea and take action.

Compare reports before presenting a conclusion

If the channel and keyword reports appear to tell different stories, check their filters and coverage. A country-level search report may cover a narrower set of visits than an overall traffic report. Write down the difference and choose the report that matches the question. When presenting your findings, include the date and market so readers can repeat the comparison and understand what the figures describe.

Frequently asked questions

Can Similarweb show the exact traffic of a competing website?

Similarweb provides estimates for website comparisons. A competitor’s own analytics account is the direct source for that site's measured visits. Use estimates to find patterns and prioritize questions you can investigate.

Can I see where competitor traffic comes from?

Available reports can show traffic channels and geography. Check the coverage, settings, and limits for the offer you are considering. Use the same country and period to make the comparison clearer.

Is Similarweb useful for a freelance SEO or small business?

It can help when you want to compare markets, channels, or search competitors. Start with one client or website and a small number of domains. Confirm that the reports you need are available before choosing an access plan.

What should I verify with a Similarweb shared account?

Check access instructions, included reports, geography, historical coverage, export options, usage limits, and support. If you need a named seat or private projects, verify how the offer handles those requirements before using it for client work.
